# local 0006: mcs51: Branching Range Exceeded after peephole rule 257.c replaces sjmp by ljmp between a short jump and its label

- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17200
- Recommended action: Apply the patch. Confirm its cost under Decision: 1 byte for some ljmp that could be sjmp, 3 bytes for some conditional jumps.
- Patch: [local-0006.patch](../../patches/local-0006.patch), commit [`ccfd2dbdb`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/ccfd2dbdb7e879a86b99f35e4691f0fc209a0664). Applies to r17200 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

On r17176, `sdcc -mmcs51 -c r2.c` gives `r2.asm:219: Error: <a> Branching Range Exceeded.` for the
file below. Line 219 is `jb _bt,00115$`, the jump at the end of the loop, and it ends 130 bytes
after its label. With `--no-peep` the file assembles. It also assembles with the medium, large,
and huge models, where the statements `g = n;` have another size.

```c
#define CASE(n) case n: bt2 = 1; break;
#define FN8 fn (); fn (); fn (); fn (); fn (); fn (); fn (); fn ();

volatile __bit bt, bt2;
volatile unsigned char g;
void fn (void);

void h (unsigned char x, unsigned char y) __reentrant
{
  do
    {
      if (y)
        {
          switch (x)
            {
            CASE (3) CASE (13) CASE (23) CASE (33) CASE (43) CASE (53)
            CASE (63) CASE (73) CASE (83) CASE (93) CASE (103)
            }
          return;
        }
      g = 20;
      g = 21;
      g = 22;
    }
  while (bt);
  FN8 FN8 FN8 FN8 FN8
}
```

## Cause

`peepHole` in `src/SDCCpeeph.c` applies each rule to all lines before it tries the next rule.
Rule 112.b replaces `ljmp` by `sjmp` when `labelInRange` accepts the distance, and rules 108.a to
108.e join an `sjmp` with the conditional jump in front of it. Later in `src/mcs51/peeph.def`,
rule 257.c replaces `sjmp %5` by `ljmp %6` when the instruction at `%5` is an unconditional jump
to `%6`. It does not have a range condition, and the short jumps across its line are not checked
again. Here each `break` is a jump to the `return` statement, which is a jump to the end of the
function, where `__reentrant` functions with a parameter on the stack have more than a `ret`.
Rule 112.b makes 10 of these jumps `sjmp`, the `jb` is then 120 bytes from its label, and rule
257.c adds 10 bytes. r16761 changed this rule from `sjmp %6` with `labelInRange(%6)` to
`ljmp %6`, and r16836 added the `sjmp` form again as rule 257.b.

## Fix

`instructionSize` in `src/mcs51/main.c` returns 3 for `sjmp`, which is the size of the `ljmp`
that rule 257.c can put in its place. `labelInRange` and `labelJTInRange` get this size through
`pcDistance`. They accept a distance only if it is still in range when rule 257.c replaces every
`sjmp` in it. The rules are unchanged.

## Decision

Jumps whose distance is in range with 2 bytes per `sjmp` and out of range with 3 stay long. That
costs 1 byte for an `ljmp` that could be an `sjmp` and 3 bytes for a conditional jump over an
`ljmp`. The regression suite was measured with and without this patch and the patches for local
0002 and local 0004 together, with the libraries compiled by the compiler under test. Its code
grows by 35 bytes for mcs51-small, 26 for mcs51-medium, 131 for mcs51-large, and 239 for
mcs51-huge. With `--stack-auto` it grows by 521 bytes for the small model and by 558 for the
large model. The 558 bytes are 0.005% of the suite's code. The two `--stack-auto` figures were
not separated from the variation of `printf_large.c` that the entry of bug #2672 describes under
Verification.

Three alternatives were measured on mcs51-huge. The libraries were not compiled again for these
runs, and on that basis the patch costs 23 bytes. Without rule 257.c the code is 28018 bytes
larger. With a copy of rule 257.a in front of rule 112.b in addition, it is 972 bytes larger, and
with copies of rules 108.a to 108.e for `ljmp` as well, 721 bytes. A condition for rule 257.c
that checks every short jump across its line would avoid the cost. It needs a new function of
about 60 lines in `src/SDCCpeeph.c` and was not written.

Rule 250.a creates an `sjmp` that the range checks before it do not count with 3 bytes. Rule
257.c does not replace that `sjmp`, because `notInJumpTable()` is false for its line, which does
not have an iCode. The patch depends on that condition.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/jump-range.c` has three `__reentrant` functions with a loop around a
`switch` of 11 cases, and their loop lengths are 6 bytes apart. On r17192 the test gets
"Branching Range Exceeded" for mcs51 with the small, medium, large, and huge models and with
`--stack-auto` for the small and large models. With the patch and the earlier patches of this
report, it passes on these six variants and on host, and the file above assembles.

With the series of this report up to the patch for local 0004 applied to r17192, the regression
suite has 0 failures for host, the six mcs51 variants, stm8, and ucz80. The diagnostics suite has
0 failures for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8. Against the series without
the three patches that Decision names, the assembly of the regression tests differs in 11 to 17
files per mcs51 variant, and each difference is a jump that stays long.

## Related

Bug #3843 reports this assembler message for other causes. Its two patches do not change
`src/mcs51/peeph.def`.
